levels.title: Match songs to label info (INNER JOIN)
levels.task: At Stellar Sound, album labels live in album_info. Join it to the chart: show only track_name then label for song ids 1001 through 1005. Use INNER JOIN on album_name. Sort by track_name A–Z. This site checks only your last SELECT—same column order and spelling as the answer.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT t.track_name, a.label ... INNER JOIN ... WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005 ORDER BY t.track_name
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name, a.label
FROM top_songs t
INNER JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY t.track_name;
levels.hintMessage: First column track_name, second label. JOIN on album_name. ORDER BY t.track_name.
levels.successMessage: Great! INNER JOIN shows only songs that have a match in both tables.

levels.title: Count INNER JOIN rows
levels.task: Same song ids 1001–1005. Write one query with one column named match_count: count how many rows you get from INNER JOIN top_songs to album_info on album_name. The correct number is 3.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM top_songs t INNER JOIN album_info a ...
levels.solution:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS match_count
FROM top_songs t
INNER JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005;
levels.hintMessage: The column name must be match_count. No extra columns. No ORDER BY.
levels.successMessage: Right! Three songs in that group have a matching album row.

levels.title: See missing labels (LEFT JOIN)
levels.task: Stellar Sound still uses ids 1001–1005 for training. LEFT JOIN album_info to top_songs on album_name. Show track_name and a second column named label (write a.label AS label). Sort by track_name. If there is no label row, the second cell is empty (NULL).
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT t.track_name, a.label AS label FROM top_songs t LEFT JOIN ...
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name, a.label AS label
FROM top_songs t
LEFT JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY t.track_name;
levels.hintMessage: Second column must be named label (use AS label). ORDER BY t.track_name. Five rows expected.
levels.successMessage: Good—LEFT JOIN keeps every song even when the label table has no match.

levels.title: Count LEFT JOIN rows
levels.task: Same ids 1001–1005, same LEFT JOIN on album_name. One SELECT, one column left_join_rows = COUNT(*). You should get 5.
levels.initialCode: -- SELECT COUNT(*) AS left_join_rows FROM top_songs t LEFT JOIN album_info a ...
levels.solution:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS left_join_rows
FROM top_songs t
LEFT JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005;
levels.hintMessage: Name the count left_join_rows. One number, one row. No ORDER BY.
levels.successMessage: Yes! LEFT JOIN keeps all five songs—even when the label is missing.

levels.title: Friendly labels with CASE
levels.task: Still at Stellar Sound, ids 1001–1005: show track_name and a column label. If the label is missing, show exactly the text 'No label info' (copy spelling). If it exists, show the real label. Use LEFT JOIN and CASE ... END AS label. Sort by track_name.
levels.initialCode: -- CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name,
  CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label
FROM top_songs t
LEFT JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY t.track_name;
levels.hintMessage: CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label. Copy the words exactly. ORDER BY t.track_name.
levels.successMessage: Perfect! Now bosses can read the sheet without seeing blank cells.
